sentences.text: Researchers investigated whether the RIM protein is required equally at synapses with different natural release probabilities by silencing specific nerve inputs in fruit flies using a neurotoxin. They found that removing RIM stopped nerve signals at fast, high-release synapses but did not stop signals at nearby slow, low-release synapses.

High-resolution images showed the protein sits closer to calcium channels at fast synapses than at slow ones, where it helps rearrange these channels to increase vesicle readiness during short-term strengthening but is not needed for long-term strengthening at the slow site.
The authors note that understanding how RIM functions at synapses with varying release rates has been difficult to resolve before this work.
